title: Precision GNSS Receiver
description: The split between what BRIEF.md fixes and what it leaves open. Every fixed_requirements entry carries the verbatim brief text that substantiates it, bound to the recorded brief digest. An open_decisions entry is a choice for the design agent: record it in 'chosen' with 'rationale', and never move it into fixed_requirements. Missing details are design freedom, not permission to fabricate unstated user requirements.

brief.authority: supplied by the benchmark; authoritative; preserved byte for byte and never edited

derivation.method: BRIEF.md was read and split; no design decision was taken. Every fixed_requirements entry, and every spec-table row sourced from the brief, carries a quotation that was checked by literal substring match against the brief bytes digested above. The build refuses to emit this file if any quotation is not found.
derivation.where_the_quotations_are: Every one of them is in this file: fixed_requirements[].brief_evidence and brief_spec_rows[].brief_evidence. The count above is the sum of those two lists, so it is recomputable from this repository alone - re-read BRIEF.md and check each string is a substring of it. brief_spec_rows carries the quotations behind the README's spec table, which would otherwise cite the brief with the evidence left in a build script.
derivation.review: two rounds of adversarial review against the brief, looking for invented requirements, lost requirements, evidence supporting a weaker claim than the one made beside it, and worksheet questions that presuppose their own answer

fixed_requirements.requirement: Provide a connector for an external active antenna (the antenna is off-board and, being active, needs DC power from this board).

fixed_requirements.requirement: Provide SAW/filtering and low-noise amplification in the receive chain, scoped and justified against what the selected GNSS module/IC actually requires.

fixed_requirements.brief_evidence: **Primary stressors:** GNSS RF chain, 50-ohm routing, LNA/filter, quiet supplies

open_decisions.decision: Which GNSS receiver to use — a pre-certified module versus a bare receiver IC — and which specific part.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief refers only to "the selected GNSS module/IC" and never names or constrains a part; it explicitly defers the choice to the designer.

open_decisions.decision: Which constellations, frequency bands and single- versus multi-band operation the receiver must support.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief calls the board "GNSS" without naming constellations or bands, and states no accuracy, fix-time or sensitivity target.

open_decisions.decision: Whether a discrete external LNA and/or SAW filter is actually required, how many stages, and their order relative to each other and to the ESD device.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief affirmatively lists "SAW/filtering and low-noise amplification" but qualifies them "as appropriate to the selected GNSS module/IC", so the topology is contingent on a part not yet chosen — the module may already integrate some or all of it, or may require all of it externally.

open_decisions.decision: Antenna connector family, gender, mount style and orientation (edge versus vertical).
open_decisions.why_open: The brief requires "an external active-antenna connector" but names no connector type or mechanical arrangement.

open_decisions.decision: ESD protection device class, capacitance budget and its placement in the RF path.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief names ESD protection as something to handle and says nothing about the device, its capacitance, or the ESD level to survive.

open_decisions.decision: Bias-feed topology — how DC reaches the antenna (over the RF conductor via a choke/ferrite/integrated bias-tee, on a separate conductor, or from a bias pin the chosen part provides), whether a DC block is needed ahead of the receiver input, the bias voltage and current, and whether short-circuit/over-current protection or bias sensing is included.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief requires a "bias feed" only, with no injection method, no blocking arrangement and no protection named; the antenna's bias voltage and current draw are properties of an antenna the brief does not specify.

open_decisions.decision: How the required USB-C output is realised — native receiver USB, or a USB-to-serial bridge — which USB-C port role the board therefore takes, the CC termination that role requires, and any USB data-rate class.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief requires "USB-C and UART output" but does not say how the USB data path is produced, and names no USB speed, port role or CC arrangement.

open_decisions.decision: UART electrical level and physical presentation: logic-level versus transceiver-driven, connector or header type, pinout, default baud rate and message format.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief requires "UART output" and fixes no level, connector, pin order or rate.

open_decisions.decision: Backup supply element (primary cell, rechargeable cell, supercapacitor, or host-supplied rail), its charge/isolation circuit, and the retention duration to design for.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief requires a "backup supply for ephemeris/RTC retention" but names no element, no retention time, and no charging behaviour.

open_decisions.decision: Electrical form of the status timing output: what signal it carries, whether it is buffered or level-translated, and whether it lands on an LED, a header, or a connector.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief requires a "status timing output" and defines neither the signal nor the physical interface.

open_decisions.decision: Power architecture: input source(s), rail voltages and count, LDO versus switching regulator per rail, sequencing, and how "quiet supply" is achieved and measured for the RF section.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief is silent on power topology, input sources and voltages; it constrains only that switching regulators must be isolated from the RF path.

open_decisions.decision: Stackup and geometry that realise the controlled impedance: dielectric materials and heights, copper weights, which layer carries the RF trace, reference-plane assignment, trace/gap geometry, and the impedance tolerance to hold.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief body says only "impedance controlled" and states no tolerance; the header's stressor list names 50-ohm routing, so the impedance in play is identified, but no stackup, dielectric height, copper weight, trace geometry or tolerance is given anywhere, and metadata supplies only a likely layer count of 4.

open_decisions.decision: Board outline, dimensions, mounting-hole pattern, connector edge placement and any enclosure or keep-out constraints.
open_decisions.why_open: Neither the brief nor the metadata states any mechanical dimension or mounting requirement.

open_decisions.decision: Whether any local MCU, configuration storage, or host processing exists on the board at all, versus a receiver that talks straight out over USB-C/UART.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief describes interfaces and an RF chain but never mentions a controller or firmware.

open_decisions.decision: Shielding strategy: shield can or fence over the RF section, ground-stitch pitch, guard structures, and RF keep-out extent.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief demands isolation from clocks and switchers but prescribes no mechanism for achieving it.

open_decisions.decision: Test, bring-up and RF verification provisions: test points, RF measurement access, programming/debug interface, and how the impedance and isolation claims will be checked.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief says nothing about test access or verification method.

open_decisions.decision: Operating environment: temperature range, supply-input range, and any EMC/regulatory regime the board must meet.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief states no environmental, supply or compliance conditions.

open_decisions.decision: Assembly process constraints: single- versus double-sided placement, minimum package sizes, and any hand-assembly or panelisation requirements.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief imposes no process or DFM constraints.
